The external carotid artery, however, lies deep to the posterior belly of digastric; while it forms part of the deep boundary, it is not typically considered a content of the anterior digastric triangle.
questions.keyConcept: External carotid artery is not a content of the anterior digastric triangle.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: As regards boundaries of carotid triangle, choose the INCORRECT matching:
questions.explanation: The carotid triangle is bounded superiorly by the posterior belly of the digastric muscle and stylohyoid, posteriorly by the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, and anteroinferiorly by the superior belly of the omohyoid. Its floor is formed by the hyoglossus, thyrohyoid, and pharyngeal constrictor muscles. The roof is formed by the investing layer of deep cervical fascia. Therefore, stating that the roof is the hyoglossus muscle is anatomically incorrect.
questions.keyConcept: Roof of carotid triangle = investing fascia; floor = hyoglossus, thyrohyoid, constrictors.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: All the following are branches of external carotid artery within the carotid triangle EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Within the carotid triangle, the external carotid artery gives off several branches: superior thyroid, lingual, facial, ascending pharyngeal, and occipital arteries. The posterior auricular artery, however, arises from the external carotid artery near the posterior belly of the digastric muscle, usually above the level of the carotid triangle proper.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior auricular artery arises above carotid triangle, not within it.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Cervical plexus gives muscular branches to all the following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The cervical plexus (C1-C4) gives muscular branches to the scalene muscles, sternocleidomastoid (with accessory nerve contribution), trapezius (with accessory nerve contribution), levator scapulae (dorsal scapular nerve + C3-C4), and infrahyoid muscles via the ansa cervicalis. The mylohyoid, however, is supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3) via the nerve to mylohyoid, not by the cervical plexus.
questions.keyConcept: Mylohyoid is supplied by mandibular nerve (CN V3), NOT cervical plexus.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The anterior triangle of the neck, include the following Except one:
questions.explanation: The occipital triangle is located in the posterior triangle of the neck, not the anterior triangle. The anterior triangle boundaries are: sternocleidomastoid (posterior), sternohyoid (anterior), and superior border of mandible (superior).
questions.keyConcept: Anterior triangle of neck is bounded by sternocleidomastoid, sternohyoid, and mandible; contains carotid, muscular, digastric, and submental triangles.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nerves supplying the scalp is derived from dorsal rami of spinal nerves?
questions.explanation: The greater occipital nerve (C2 dorsal ramus) is the only scalp nerve derived from dorsal rami of spinal nerves; all other listed nerves are derived from ventral rami (cervical plexus).
questions.keyConcept: Greater occipital nerve dorsal ramus origin

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The posterior triangle of the neck
options: Is bordered by sternocleidomastoid, mandible and trapezius
Has the accessory nerve beneath fascia of its floor
Is roofed by prevertebral layer of fascia
Contains trunks of the brachial plexus
questions.explanation: The posterior triangle is bounded by sternocleidomastoid, trapezius, and clavicle (not mandible); it is roofed by the superficial fascia and prevertebral layer of deep cervical fascia.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior triangle boundaries and roof

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The anterior triangle of the neck, include the following
questions.explanation: The anterior triangle has four subdivisions (muscular, carotid, digastric, submental); the occipital triangle is part of the posterior triangle, not anterior triangle.
questions.keyConcept: Anterior triangle subdivisions

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following muscles subdivides the posterior triangle of the neck:
questions.explanation: The inferior belly of the omohyoid muscle subdivides the posterior triangle into an occipital triangle (above) and a supraclavicular triangle (below). The sternocleidomastoid forms the anterior border; the superior belly of omohyoid is within the anterior triangle.
questions.keyConcept: Inferior belly of omohyoid subdivides posterior triangle into two parts

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The following structures form the floor of the posterior triangle of the neck Except:
options: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia.
Prevertebral layer of deep cervical fascia.
questions.explanation: The floor of the posterior triangle is formed by the levator scapulae, splenius capitis, and scalenus medius muscles, covered by the prevertebral layer of deep cervical fascia. The investing layer surrounds the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid, not forming the floor.
questions.keyConcept: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia is NOT part of floor of posterior triangle - EXCEPTION

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The vein running along the roof of the posterior triangle of the neck drains into which vein?
questions.explanation: The external jugular vein drains the posterior triangle of the neck and empties into the subclavian vein (or sometimes the internal jugular vein at the root of the neck).
questions.keyConcept: External jugular vein drains posterior triangle and joins subclavian vein.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Which nerve provides cutaneous innervation to the skin overlying the angle of the mandible?
questions.explanation: The great auricular nerve (from C2-C3 cervical plexus) provides cutaneous innervation to the skin overlying the angle of the mandible and parotid region.
questions.keyConcept: Great auricular nerve (C2-C3) supplies sensation over the mandibular angle and parotid area.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Which structure is located within the carotid sheath?
questions.explanation: The carotid sheath contains the common/internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein, and vagus nerve (CN X). It extends from the carotid bifurcation to the root of the neck.
questions.keyConcept: Carotid sheath contains ICA, IJV, and CN X - a true fascial investment of the neck vessels.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The great auricular nerve carries fibers from:
questions.explanation: The great auricular nerve arises from C2-C3 ventral rami (cervical plexus) and supplies the skin of the ear and adjacent scalp.
questions.keyConcept: Great auricular nerve: C2 and C3 ventral rami.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Skin over the angle of the mandible is supplied by ……… nerve.
questions.explanation: The great auricular nerve (C2-C3) supplies the skin over the angle of the mandible and lower ear region as part of cervical plexus distribution.
questions.keyConcept: Angle of mandible: great auricular nerve (C2-C3).

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Infection in the area of chin leads to enlargement of ……… lymph nodes.
questions.explanation: The submental lymph nodes drain the chin and lower lip midline, lying beneath the chin in the submental triangle.
questions.keyConcept: Chin infection: submental lymph nodes enlarge.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: An infrahyoid muscle supplied directly by C1 ventral ramus is:
questions.explanation: The thyrohyoid muscle is innervated directly by C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve. Other infrahyoid muscles receive ansa cervicalis (C1-3).
questions.keyConcept: Thyrohyoid: directly by C1 via hypoglossal nerve.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: A branch from external carotid artery running in both carotid and digastric triangles is ……… artery.
questions.explanation: The facial artery runs through both carotid triangle (origin from ECA) and digastric triangle (before entering face), giving off branches like submental, superior labial, and lateral nasal.
questions.keyConcept: Facial artery: runs through both carotid and digastric triangles.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The carotid sheath encloses:
questions.explanation: The carotid sheath contains the common/internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein, and vagus nerve throughout its course in the neck.
questions.keyConcept: Carotid sheath: contains CCA/ICA, IJV, and vagus nerve.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: A nerve embedded in the roof of the posterior triangle of the neck and crossing the triangle parallel to levator scapulae is:
questions.explanation: The spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) crosses the posterior triangle embedded in its roof, running from the sternocleidomastoid to the trapezius, parallel to levator scapulae.
questions.keyConcept: Spinal accessory nerve: crosses posterior triangle parallel to levator scapulae.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: A nerve related to anterior aspect of anterior scalene muscle is:
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve runs on the anterior surface of the anterior scalene muscle, making it vulnerable during scalene blocks and relevant in interscalene anesthesia.
questions.keyConcept: Phrenic nerve: anterior aspect of anterior scalene muscle.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The main opener of the mouth is:
questions.explanation: The lateral pterygoid is the main mouth opener, pulling the mandibular neck forward and down; gravity and suprahyoid muscles assist.
questions.keyConcept: Lateral pterygoid: main opener of mouth.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The external carotid artery crosses ……… triangles of the neck.
questions.explanation: The external carotid artery runs through the carotid triangle after originating in the neck, with branches emerging from its anterior, posterior, and medial surfaces.
questions.keyConcept: External carotid crosses carotid triangle of neck.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The muscle supplied by C1 through hypoglossal nerve is the:
questions.explanation: The thyrohyoid muscle is supplied by C1 spinal nerve fibers that travel with the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) as the nerve to thyrohyoid. This is an exception to the rule that infrahyoid muscles are supplied by ansa cervicalis.
questions.keyConcept: Thyrohyoid is supplied by C1 via hypoglossal nerve (nerve to thyrohyoid).

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: The following are branches of the vagus nerve in the neck Except:
questions.explanation: The vagus nerve gives several branches in the neck: pharyngeal branch, superior laryngeal nerve, recurrent laryngeal nerve (left and right), and cardiac branches. The carotid body and carotid sinus, however, receive their sensory innervation from the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) via the branch of Hering (carotid branch), NOT from the vagus nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Branches to carotid body are from glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), NOT vagus.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Regarding the spinal accessory nerve; all are true Except:
options: Arises entirely from the spinal cord.
Enters the skull via the foramen magnum.
Leaves the skull via the jugular foramen.
Contributes to the pharyngeal plexus of nerves.
Its injury in the posterior triangle results in wasting of the trapezius on the same side.
questions.explanation: The spinal accessory nerve arises from the spinal cord (C1-C6/7), enters the cranial cavity through the foramen magnum, and exits via the jugular foramen. It supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius. It does NOT contribute to the pharyngeal plexus of nerves; this plexus is formed by glossopharyngeal (CN IX), vagus (CN X), and sympathetic fibers.
questions.keyConcept: Spinal accessory nerve does NOT contribute to the pharyngeal plexus.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: Accessory nerve supplies which of the following muscles?
questions.explanation: The accessory nerve (CN XI) is traditionally described as supplying two muscles: sternocleidomastoid (upper part of neck) and trapezius (posterior neck and shoulder). Some sources also describe supply to levator scapulae, but standard dental and gross anatomy teaches that accessory nerve innervates sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
questions.keyConcept: Accessory nerve supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: All the following muscles are supplied by the hypoglossal nerve Except:
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) supplies all intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue except the palatoglossus (supplied by the vagus nerve). This includes genioglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus, and all intrinsic tongue muscles. The anterior belly of the digastric, however, is supplied by the mandibular nerve (CN V3) via the nerve to mylohyoid, not by the hypoglossal nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Anterior belly of digastric is supplied by mandibular nerve (V3), NOT hypoglossal nerve.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: As regards accessory nerve, choose the INCORRECT statement:
options: Its cranial part arises from nucleus ambiguus.
Its spinal part unites with its cranial part at foramen ovale.
It exits from skull with vagus & glossopharyngeal nerves.
Its cranial part is distributed through pharyngeal & recurrent laryngeal nerves.
Its spinal part enters cranial cavity through foramen magnum.
questions.explanation: The spinal accessory nerve has a cranial part arising from the nucleus ambiguus (joining the vagus and exiting via jugular foramen) and a spinal part arising from the anterior horn cells of C1-C5, entering the skull through the foramen magnum, and exiting via the jugular foramen. The spinal part does NOT unite with the cranial part at the foramen ovale; rather, the cranial part exits with the glossopharyngeal and vagus through the jugular foramen, and the spinal part also exits through the jugular foramen but courses independently to supply the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
questions.keyConcept: Spinal accessory does NOT unite with cranial part at foramen ovale; both exit via jugular foramen.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: A patient that had trauma to the spinal accessory nerve is expected to suffer from:
options: Paralysis of muscles of the lower part of the face
Deviation of the tongue towards the damaged side
Deviation of the tongue towards the healthy side
questions.explanation: The spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) innervates the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles. Damage causes inability to shrug the shoulder (trapezius) and difficulty rotating the head (sternocleidomastoid).
questions.keyConcept: CN XI supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius for neck rotation and shoulder abduction.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.question: A lesion of the spinal accessory nerve causes paralysis of:
questions.explanation: CN XI supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
questions.keyConcept: Spinal accessory nerve: sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.
